ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a trapezoid, with the upper base shorter and the lower base longer, and the left and right sides are slanted sides. The gray rectangle is located in the lower half of the trapezoid, the bottom side of the rectangle lies on the lower base of the trapezoid, and the top side of the rectangle is a horizontal line, connecting points X and Y on the two slanted sides of the trapezoid. The problem states that X and Y are the midpoints of the two legs of the trapezoid. Reasoning: The segment XY connecting the midpoints of the two legs of the trapezoid is the midline of the trapezoid; it is parallel to the two bases, and its length equals the average of the lengths of the upper and lower bases. Let the height of the trapezoid be h, and the length of XY be m; then the area of the trapezoid equals m × h. Since X and Y are the midpoints of the two legs, XY is located at half the height of the trapezoid, so the height of the gray rectangle is h/2, and the width is m. Therefore the area of the gray rectangle is m × h/2. It is known that the area of the gray rectangle is 13 cm², so the area of the trapezoid is 2 times it: 2 × 13 = 26 cm².

raw_record.question_text: The area of the grey rectangle shown on the right is $13 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$. X and Y are the midpoints of the sides of the trapezium. How big is the area of the trapezium?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the grey rectangle has its top side along the horizontal segment joining X and Y, and its bottom side on the lower base of the trapezium. X and Y lie on the two sloping sides and are stated to be midpoints. Use the midpoint property in a trapezium: the segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides is parallel to the bases, has length equal to the average of the two bases, and lies halfway up the height. Therefore the grey rectangle has width equal to the trapezium’s midline length and height equal to half the trapezium’s height. Since trapezium area = midline length × full height, while grey rectangle area = midline length × half height, the trapezium area is twice the rectangle area: 2 × 13 = 26 cm^2.
